ART-END-WHAT-IS-HERALDRY-SKIRMISH.identity: Two rival adventurers of the Dying Lands who have reached the same iron-bound treasure chest in a monster-haunted ruin at the same moment, while a Monster closes in behind them: the competitive PvPvE race for treasure in miniature.
ART-END-WHAT-IS-HERALDRY-SKIRMISH.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Low three-quarter view: the chest sits at the centre on cracked flagstones, one rival crouched at each end with a hand on its ring handle; a broken wall stub rises behind the chest, and over its top reaches a single long clawed Monster arm, shape only.
details: Iron-bound wooden treasure chest, lid still shut, corner straps rusted, one ring handle at each end
Left rival: a Human in a battered ring shirt, shortsword half-drawn, one gauntleted hand on the handle
Right rival: a lean Elf in a leather coat, dagger reversed in the free hand, the other hand on the opposite handle
Neither looks at the other's face: both stare at the clawed arm coming over the wall
Knee-high broken wall stub with moss and a fallen capstone, the clawed arm drawn in solid black
A few coins spilled from a split seam, hatched dull with no stamps
Cracked flagstones fading out in a few strokes on all sides
must: Exactly two rival figures and one chest; the Monster shows only as one clawed arm and shoulder
activity: Both rivals freeze mid-grab, each still gripping their end of the chest
The clawed arm reaches over the wall top toward them
ART-END-WHAT-IS-HERALDRY-SKIRMISH.atmosphere: Greed and dread in the same breath; the richest party is the one that bleeds.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
Do not repeat the chapter 2 sighting across a fog valley or the cover's shrine arch
No full Monster figure, face or portrait
No banners or heraldic devices
No gore
sources: Lines 165-187 (1.1): two rival adventuring parties race through monster-haunted ruins for treasure; neutral Monsters stalk the field; the richest party is often the one that bled for every coin
Lines 3719-3729 (7.10): ring shirt and leather coat are canonical Chest armour

ART-END-CORE-TERMS.identity: The three kinds of combatant the rules name, met in one crypt passage: a Dwarf Hero, the Guard Hireling at their side, and a Ghoul, the Monster that has come for them.
ART-END-CORE-TERMS.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Side view down a short vaulted crypt passage: the Dwarf Hero and the Guard stand shoulder to shoulder at left, the Ghoul crouched low at right in the passage mouth, the gap of bare floor between them the centre of the picture.
details: Dwarf Hero: very broad, short-limbed, braided beard, mail, lantern raised in one hand and handaxe in the other
Guard Hireling: human retainer in a padded coat with a heater shield and a mace, a step behind the Dwarf's shoulder
Ghoul: grey, gaunt and hook-clawed, loping low on all fours with its head thrust forward
Low barrel vault of rough stone, two niches with old bones
Lantern light shown by open white paper around the pair, the Ghoul's end of the passage in solid black
Dust and a dropped bone on the floor between them
must: Three combatants only: one Dwarf Hero, one shield-bearing Guard, one Ghoul
activity: The Dwarf and the Guard brace side by side
The Ghoul creeps forward, claws on the flagstones
ART-END-CORE-TERMS.atmosphere: Close, cold and about to break.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
Not the Undercroft room (no hidden door, no cloaked figure) and not the Shadowed Under Passage scenario
Do not draw the Ghoul as a zombie or a skeleton
No gore
sources: Lines 445-453 (2.1): combatant, Hero, Hireling and Monster defined
Lines 15578 (11.2.5): Guard Hireling with mace and heater shield
Lines 2245-2254 (6.9): Dwarf build and Darkvision
Lines 8244-8246 (9.7): Ghoul, grey, gaunt and hook-clawed, lopes in packs through tombs

ART-END-ADVANTAGES-AND-DISADVANTAGES.identity: The advantage of higher elevation: an archer kneeling on the broken top of a ruined wall, shooting down at a Beastman scrambling up the rubble below.
ART-END-ADVANTAGES-AND-DISADVANTAGES.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Low angle from the foot of the rubble slope: the wall stub rises at right with the archer kneeling on its broken top, the Beastman climbing the scree at lower left, a clear diagonal from archer to target.
details: Elf archer in a leather coat kneeling on the wall top, shortbow at full draw aimed steeply downward
Ruined wall stub with broken coursing and a jagged top edge, about twice a person's height
Beastman: hunched man-shape with a goat's head and black-clawed hands, clawing up loose rubble
Loose stones sliding from under the Beastman's feet
A spent arrow standing in the rubble near the Beastman
Weeds in the wall joints
must: The archer is clearly well above the Beastman
activity: The archer looses downward
The Beastman claws upward, slipping
ART-END-ADVANTAGES-AND-DISADVANTAGES.atmosphere: Hard, cold advantage taken without mercy.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
No longbow, staff or plate armour on the archer
Not the aqueduct of the chapter 4 opener
No gore
sources: Lines 531-551 (2.4): Advantage and Disadvantage; attacker at a higher elevation gains Advantage
Lines 7866-7868 (9.7): Beastman, hunched man-shape with goat or boar head and black claws
Line 3693 (7.9): Shortbow is a two-handed Ranged weapon

ART-END-ACTION-POINTS-AND-SUMMONS.identity: An Infernal Imp, a Sorcerer's temporary Summon, unravelling into smoke and cinders as it is dispelled from the world.
ART-END-ACTION-POINTS-AND-SUMMONS.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Eye-level view of a single fallen column drum; the imp crouches on top of it at the centre, its lower body and one wing already coming apart into curling smoke that drifts off to the right and thins to nothing.
details: Knee-high, bat-winged imp with a barbed tail, small clawed hands and a snarling face
One wing intact and spread, the other shredding into smoke strands and flicked cinder flecks
Tail and legs dissolving from the tips inward
Fallen column drum with a cracked fluting, the imp's claws gripping its edge
A faint scorch ring on the stone where it was called
Smoke drawn in a few bold broken curves, not as grey haze
must: Only the imp and the column drum; no caster in frame
activity: The imp twists to look at its own vanishing wing
ART-END-ACTION-POINTS-AND-SUMMONS.atmosphere: Brief, spiteful and borrowed; nothing summoned stays.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
Not the Sun-Drowned Imp bestiary portrait: no tomb setting, no flying pose
No glow, grey wash or airbrushed smoke
No summoning circle with symbols
sources: Lines 568-592 (2.5): Summons are temporary; a third Summon dispels one; Summons are removed at the end of the adventure
Lines 3159-3175 (6.13 Sorcerer): Infernal Imp Summon, Small, Fly, Fiend, fire
Line 9391 (9.7): imp, knee-high and bat-winged with a barbed tail

ART-END-TERRAIN.identity: A small stretch of Dying Lands ground that holds every kind of terrain a party must read: a shallow ford, a deep channel, a fallen column, a thorn hedge and a rubble field, with no one in it.
ART-END-TERRAIN.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Slightly raised three-quarter view: a stream crosses the picture, a broken imperial column lies across it as a footbridge at the centre, stepping stones in the shallows to one side and a dark deep pool to the other; a thorn hedge and rubble frame the near bank.
details: Fallen fluted column lying across the stream, moss on its top, one end resting on a statue base
Shallow ford with stepping stones and ripples drawn in short broken strokes
Deep channel below the column drawn as a solid black pool
Reeds and a thorn hedge on the near bank
Scatter of rubble blocks and a broken capital
Mud bank with a single boot print
must: No figures and no creatures
ART-END-TERRAIN.atmosphere: Quiet ground that will cost time, footing or blood to cross.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
Not the chapter 1 pass, the Greenmark climate road or the Mire walkway
No bridge of planks, no buildings
No square grid or measured lines
sources: Lines 828-864 (2.9.1): Terrain Types and standard assignments: fords and streams Shallow Water, rivers Deep Water, fallen pillars and broken columns Impassable, hedges and thorn barriers Cover, rubble fields Difficult
Lines 919-938 (2.9.6-2.9.7): Shallow Water and Deep Water

ART-END-PARTY-PHASE.identity: Two Heroes of one party taking turns at a ruined corner: one dashes across an open gap while the other waits behind cover with a loaded crossbow, holding back for whatever answers.
ART-END-PARTY-PHASE.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Three-quarter view of a broken corner of wall: the waiting Hero kneels behind it in the foreground with the crossbow levelled past the edge, the running Hero is mid-stride in the open gap beyond, smaller.
details: Kneeling Hero in a gambeson with a light crossbow braced on the wall edge, finger off the trigger
Running Hero in a leather coat, low and fast, shortsword in hand, cloak flying
Corner of a ruined wall with a fallen lintel
Open gap of cracked paving between the two
A spent bolt and a dropped glove by the kneeling Hero's knee
must: Two Heroes only, clearly on the same side
activity: One Hero crosses the gap
The other holds still, watching for the reply
ART-END-PARTY-PHASE.atmosphere: Measured, patient, every breath spent with care.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
No enemies in frame
Not the chapter 3 dawn gathering
No banners
sources: Lines 1043-1096 (3.3): sides alternate activations; unspent AP is kept for Reactions
Lines 1207-1229 (4.2): Wait holds remaining AP for Reactions
Line 3698 (7.9): Light Crossbow

ART-END-MONSTER-PHASE.identity: A Goblin mob of the Greenmark waking and pouring over the top of a ruined steading wall at night, the moment a Monster Group activates.
ART-END-MONSTER-PHASE.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Front view of a low wall top running across the picture: a dense knot of goblins spills over it at the centre, more heads and blades behind, the knot thinning to a few stragglers at each end.
details: Knee-high, green-grey, all elbows and malice: six to eight goblins in a tight mass
Notched blades raised, two swinging slings of river stones
Wide eyes and bared teeth catching small white highlights
Rough stone wall top with a broken thatch edge from the steading behind
Night shown by solid black behind the mob, white paper below the wall
One goblin tumbling head first over the wall
must: The mob reads as one mass, not as separate portraits
activity: The goblins surge over the wall all at once
ART-END-MONSTER-PHASE.atmosphere: Sudden, chittering and overwhelming; singly cowards, in numbers a tide.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
Not the Goblin bestiary portrait: no single isolated goblin
No goblin shaman, no bugbear
No gore
sources: Lines 1098-1126 (3.4): Monster Groups wake and activate in order during the Monster Phase
Lines 7849-7851 (9.7): Goblin, knee-high, green-grey, notched blade and sling of river stones, infesting ruined steadings in mobs, a tide in numbers

ART-END-ACTION-BASICS.identity: A Hero at the foot of a cellar stair letting a lit torch fall to free a hand, drawing a blade as shapes stir in the dark ahead.
ART-END-ACTION-BASICS.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Low view at the bottom of a short stone stair: the Hero stands at the centre with the torch tumbling from one hand toward the floor and the other hand pulling a sword from its scabbard; the passage beyond is a block of solid black with two vague shapes.
details: Human Hero in a hooded mantle and leather coat, weight on the back foot
Torch mid-fall, its flame drawn as a few clean ink tongues
Shortsword halfway out of a worn scabbard
Worn cellar stair behind, three or four steps
Two indistinct hunched shapes in the black passage, no features
Torchlight as a ring of open paper on the floor
must: One Hero only; the shapes stay vague
activity: The Hero drops the torch and draws in one movement
ART-END-ACTION-BASICS.atmosphere: A heartbeat of decision in the dark.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
No detailed Monster
Not the Undercroft or the Shadowed Under Passage
No glow effect around the torch
sources: Lines 1191-1205 (4.1): actions in any order; a combatant may speak, signal, and drop non-objective held items without spending AP
Line 4652 (7.16): Torch, a carried Light Source

ART-END-UNIVERSAL-ACTIONS.identity: The Push: a Dwarf Hero driving a shield into an Orc raider and shoving them back toward a broken balustrade.
ART-END-UNIVERSAL-ACTIONS.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Side view on a short stretch of ruined terrace: the Dwarf at left with shoulder behind a round shield, the Orc at right rocked backward off balance, their heels at the broken edge, open air beyond.
details: Dwarf: very broad and heavy, braided beard, mail, round shield braced with the shoulder, handaxe held back
Orc: broad as a doorway, grey-skinned, heavy-jawed, lower tusks jutting, battleaxe and shield flung wide
Broken stone balustrade with missing balusters behind the Orc
Terrace paving cracked, one slab tilting
Dust kicked up at the Dwarf's planted boots
must: The Dwarf is pushing, not striking; the Orc is falling back
activity: The Dwarf drives forward
The Orc staggers back toward the edge
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
Not the chapter 5 bridge clash and no undead
Do not give the Dwarf a greataxe or a horned helm
No gore
sources: Lines 1207-1226 (4.2): Push, a STR Check to Push an adjacent combatant 2 inches directly away
Lines 7948-7950 (9.7): Orc, broad as a doorway, battleaxe and shield, grey-skinned with lower tusks
Lines 2245-2254 (6.9): Dwarf

ART-END-MOVEMENT-RULES.identity: A Human Rogue jumping a gap between two broken rooftops in a ruined town, the street far below.
ART-END-MOVEMENT-RULES.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Side view across the gap: the take-off roof edge at left, the landing ledge at right, the Rogue in mid-air at the centre with legs tucked, the narrow street a dark slot beneath.

Left roof: broken slates and an exposed rafter
Right roof: a lower, narrow stone ledge with a cracked gutter
Dark drop between drawn in solid black and hatching
Loose slate falling from the take-off edge
Cloak streaming behind
must: The landing point is level with or below the take-off point
activity: The Rogue is airborne mid-jump

Not the chapter 4 aqueduct or a chasm in a cave

No flying or magic

ART-END-COMBAT-BASICS.identity: A Bugbear rising out of dead bracken to strike from arm's reach with its spiked morningstar, before its quarry can close.
ART-END-COMBAT-BASICS.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Three-quarter view: the Bugbear looms at left, long arm fully extended, the morningstar swinging out over the bracken toward a Hero at right who is still a full stride away with shield raised late.
details: Bugbear: seven feet of shaggy, long-armed menace, flat face, fur like dead bracken
Spiked morningstar at the end of the overlong arm
Dead bracken and undergrowth parting around the Bugbear's legs
Hero in a gambeson with a small round targe and a shortsword, one foot sliding back
Clear gap of ground between the Hero's blade and the Bugbear
must: The Bugbear's reach visibly exceeds the Hero's
activity: The Bugbear swings from beyond the Hero's reach
The Hero flinches back behind the targe
ART-END-COMBAT-BASICS.atmosphere: Ambush and the cruelty of a longer arm.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
Not the Bugbear bestiary portrait: this is a two-figure clash
No goblins
No gore
sources: Lines 1473-1484 (5.1): melee attacks, Engaged, and Reach to 2 inches
Lines 7968-7987 (9.7): Bugbear, long-armed, fur the colour of dead bracken, strikes from arm's reach with a morningstar; Long-Limbed gives Reach

ART-END-THE-ATTACK-SEQUENCE.identity: The instant of defence in an attack: two blades locked at the crossguard in a Parry, close enough to see the notches.
ART-END-THE-ATTACK-SEQUENCE.composition: Closing tailpiece at the foot of a page, printed about 2.6 to 3.3 in wide and as short as 1.6 in: one clear focal subject with a strong silhouette in the middle of the frame, generous open white paper around it, and every edge dissolving into the paper in sparse broken strokes. Close crop at chest height: two gloved hands and two crossed blades fill the centre, locked near the hilts; the fighters' arms and shoulders fade into white paper at each side.
details: Left blade: a plain longsword with a straight crossguard, held in a mailed glove
Right blade: a heavy single-edged falchion in a bare scarred fist
Blades crossed in an X near the guards, a notch biting into one edge
Sleeves: a mail cuff on one arm, a padded sleeve on the other
A few flicked sparks as ink flecks at the contact point
must: Hands and blades only; no faces
activity: Both fighters strain against the locked blades
ART-END-THE-ATTACK-SEQUENCE.atmosphere: Strain, grit and a second that decides everything.
avoid: No lettering, numbers, dice, game tokens, or rulebook pages
No full figures
No glow or motion blur
No gore
sources: Lines 1530-1540 (5.2): the Attack Sequence; Reactions declared before damage dice
Lines 1521-1528 (5.1.2): Block, Dodge and Parry

Open-faced helm caved in on one side, a rivet sprung

A split shield rim at the edge of the arrangement
